skill.name: ghe-requirements
skill.description: Manage GHE requirements documents for GitHub Elements projects, including folder structure, versioning, issue links, and SERENA backup guidance.
skill.summary: Create, version, validate, and link GHE requirements documents before development starts.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: The audit found many Markdown backtick false positives, but several bash workflow blocks remain real external-command surfaces. The highest confirmed risk is authorization to write ~/.claude settings, plus an overbroad instruction block that can weaken normal instruction hierarchy.

remediation.issue: The skill grants permission to write ~/.claude settings.
remediation.suggestion: Remove home-directory write guidance. Require explicit user approval and narrow any configuration changes to project-local files.

remediation.issue: The opening IRON LAW uses absolute language that may override normal safety and instruction hierarchy.
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite it to respect user requirements only when they do not conflict with higher-priority instructions, safety rules, or repository policy.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use variable-controlled paths, issue identifiers, and GitHub CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate IDs and paths, quote variables consistently, add dry-run guidance, and require confirmation before file writes or GitHub mutations.

content.value_statement: Feature work can drift when requirements are missing or stale. This skill defines requirement files, versioning, issue links, and backup steps.
actual_capabilities: Defines the REQUIREMENTS folder layout with templates, epic folders, wave folders, standalone files, and a changelog.
Provides a standard REQ file structure with metadata, acceptance criteria, atomic changes, tests, dependencies, and revision history.
Describes how to create, approve, version, and commit requirement files.
Shows how to link requirement documents in GitHub issue threads.
Includes validation checks for linked requirements and version drift.
Describes backup of requirement files into SERENA memory.
limitations: It provides process guidance, not an installed command-line tool.
The shell examples require local review before use in a real repository.
GitHub CLI actions require authentication and repository permissions.
It does not validate requirement quality without agent or reviewer judgment.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Requirement
use_cases.description: Create a structured requirement before development starts, with acceptance criteria, atomic changes, tests, and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Coordinate GitHub Issue Work
use_cases.description: Link GitHub development issues to the current requirement version so implementers share the same source of truth.

use_cases.title: Review Requirement Drift
use_cases.description: Compare issue links, requirement versions, and acceptance criteria before implementation review or test planning.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Requirement Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start a new feature requirement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GHE requirement draft for this feature request: [feature]. Include user story, acceptance criteria, atomic changes, tests, and dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Requirement
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: revise a requirement with version history.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this GHE requirement for a minor version change: [requirement summary]. Preserve original intent and list the revision history entry.

prompt_templates.title: Link a Requirement to an Issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare issue text from a requirement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare GitHub issue requirements text for REQ-[number] version [version]. Include the primary link, acceptance criteria, and atomic changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Requirement Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this GitHub issue against its linked GHE requirement. Identify missing links, stale versions, uncovered acceptance criteria, and unclear tests.

output_examples.input: Create a requirement for adding export filters to a reporting dashboard.
output: A draft requirement with a feature overview, user story, and acceptance criteria for filtered exports.
A proposed atomic change list covering UI controls, export behavior, and tests.
A dependency section noting related dashboard and reporting requirements.

output_examples.input: Check whether issue 42 is linked to the current REQ version.
output: A validation summary showing whether the issue includes a requirement link.
A version comparison between the issue text and the current requirement file.
A short remediation note if the issue is missing or stale.

best_practices: Confirm requirement changes with the user before changing acceptance criteria or scope.
Keep issue links tied to explicit requirement versions.
Review shell examples before running them in repositories with sensitive files.
anti_patterns: Starting development work before a requirement file exists.
Changing requirement scope without updating revision history.
Running GitHub CLI or file commands without checking paths and permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages GHE requirement documents, version history, issue links, validation checks, and backup guidance.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that an agent or user may apply after review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI access?
faq.answer: Some examples use GitHub CLI commands, so those workflows require authentication and repository permissions.

faq.question: Can it validate linked requirement versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes checks for requirement links, file existence, and version drift.

faq.question: What should users review before use?
faq.answer: Users should review file paths, shell variables, GitHub issue targets, and repository permissions before running commands.
